item.caption:
8 days. The finish line is in sight! 🗳️

Election Day is Tuesday, November 3rd. If you’re voting by mail, don’t wait on that ballot. Early voting hours are limited, so check yours and go. If you’re voting in person, know your polling place and what to bring.

Eight days is enough time, but only if you start today.

The image is a dark blue graphic with text about city measures. It displays "TENANTS TOGETHER VOTER GUIDE 2026" in yellow at the top. Below that, "CITY MEASURES" is written in large white letters. Several measures are listed with checkmarks or an "X" and descriptions of their potential impact on rent increases and evictions.

The image displays text in Spanish with a blue and yellow color scheme. It lists "ESTADO" and three propositions. "Sí a la Proposición 1" is marked with a blue checkmark, while "No a la Proposición 43" and "No a la Proposición 45" are marked with red crosses. The logo for "TENANTS TOGETHER" appears in the bottom right corner.

The image displays a guide for voters regarding local measures. It shows "Sí" (Yes) with a checkmark next to measures for Redwood City, San Pablo, and San Francisco. "No" with an "X" is marked next to a measure for Salinas. The text also includes "Tenants Together" and "Guía para el electorado 2026."

item.caption:
🗳️🇺🇸 ¡YO YA HICE MI PARTE! ¿Y TÚ, YA VOTASTE?

Hoy ejercí uno de los derechos más importantes que tenemos: hacer escuchar nuestra voz a través del voto.

Porque el futuro no se construye solamente con opiniones, sino también con acciones.

Votar es pensar en nuestras familias, en nuestros hijos, en nuestra comunidad y en las generaciones que vienen detrás de nosotros.

No importa por quién votes. Lo importante es que participes, que te informes y que tomes tu propia decisión.

La democracia se fortalece cuando todos hacemos nuestra parte.

✅ Yo ya voté. ¿Y tú, ya votaste?

🇺🇸🗳️ ¡Tu voz cuenta y tu voto también!

#YoYaVoté #IVoted #TuVotoCuenta #Houston #Texas Elecciones2026 ParticipaciónCiudadana EnriqueDeportes

author: sampositivepinoy

item.caption:
🇺🇸 I VOTED — AND I VOTED STRAIGHT RED.

Early voting for the 2026 Midterm Elections is my opportunity to make my voice heard.

Yes, high gas prices and the financial strain on family budgets matter. We feel them every time we fill up the tank, buy groceries, and pay our bills. These are serious concerns, and economic conditions can change over time.

But my vote is about more than today’s prices. It’s about the future of our country and the values we leave to the next generation.

I weighed the issues that matter most to me: border security, the threat of Islamic extremism, parental rights in decisions affecting our minor children, and the preservation of our nation’s core values.

I believe short-term financial hardships, however painful, should not overshadow the long-term direction of our country. The decisions we make today can shape our children’s future for decades.

I respect everyone’s right to vote according to their conscience. This is mine. I voted for the principles I believe will help protect our families, strengthen our nation, and preserve the values that matter to me.

My vote. My convictions. My country’s future. 🇺🇸

Please go out to vote.  Have your voice heard.  Vote straight RED.

#IVoted #EarlyVoting #Midterms2026 #StraightRed #AmericaFirst #FamilyValues #BorderSecurity

author: suzyemre

item.caption:
🇺🇸 I VOTED! 🇺🇸

Today was a little bittersweet. I just cast my ballot for the very last time as a Texas resident.

Texas has been my home for so many years, and knowing that my next election will be in North Carolina makes this one feel a little different. ❤️

I know how I hope this election turns out, but I also know that hoping isn't enough. Elections are decided by the people who show up and make their voices heard.

We may not all agree on the candidates or the issues, and that's okay. That's part of living in a democracy.

But one thing I hope we can agree on is that our voices matter, and our votes matter.

So get informed, make your choices, and VOTE!

One last ballot in the Lone Star State. 🇨🇱❤️🤍💙

Texas, it's been an honor! 🇺🇸

#IVoted #Texas #YourVoteMatters #CivicDuty #NewChapter

item.caption:
🇮🇱 Israel’s elections are almost here! Here’s everything you need to know before you vote!

Election Day is Tuesday, October 27th, and whether it’s your first time voting in Israel or you’ve done it before, there are a few important things to know to make sure your vote counts.

🗳️ Here’s the breakdown:

📍 Where to vote: Google “איתור קלפי” and use the official gov.il website to find your polling station (kalpi). Make sure to check because it might not be near where you currently live!

🕖 When: Tuesday, October 27th, from 7 AM to 10 PM. Election Day is also a national day off!

🪪 What to bring: Your original Israeli Teudat Zehut, driver’s license, or passport.

✉️ How to vote: You’ll receive an envelope, choose your party’s slip behind the voting screen, seal the envelope, and drop it into the ballot box.

⚠️ Be careful! Putting slips from different parties in the same envelope or making certain other mistakes could invalidate your vote.

🔤 Know your letters! Each party has its own Hebrew letters on the ballot, so make sure you know which ones you’re looking for.

🔗 For official election information and the full list of parties, visit bechirot.gov.il.

📌 SAVE this post so you have everything you need on Election Day, and SEND it to a friend who might be voting in Israel for the first time!

And remember: Cool people vote. 😎🇮🇱

Voting is one way we contribute to the direction of our country, and I don’t take that responsibility lightly. Especially now, when the quality of our leadership, the protection of our freedoms, and the opportunities available to future generations deserve serious consideration.

Our nation’s strength rests in leadership guided by integrity, competence, compassion, and accountability. item.caption:
Webinar TOMORROW!

Midterm Elections are NOT mid! Elections are a critical time for voters to make decisions about laws, policies, and elected leaders which will impact the lives of everyone around us.
 
Join Disability Vote California for information about the upcoming General Election on November 3. @cfilc_1982 @calscdd 

Learn more and register at the link in our bio or by visiting: tinyurl.com/DisabilityVoteCA2026

In the webinar we will cover:
 
- Accessible voting options
- The importance of voting in the midterm elections
- What's on the ballot? Races and statewide propositions
- How to get engaged in voting advocacy

Voters with disabilities have the chance to exercise their voting rights and enact change for our communities. Get informed and make your vote count by this Election Day (November 3)!

#DisabilityVoteCalifornia #CFILC #SCDD #DisabilityRightsCA #MidtermElection #ElectionDay 
.
.

item.caption:
According to statistician Nate Silver, Democrats’ odds of winning back control of the U.S. Senate have jumped from 50% to 75% with just one week left until Election Day.

Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take control. Their clearest path to controlling the chamber involves defending every seat they hold, flipping North Carolina and Maine, and winning two more Republican-held seats in states President Trump carried by double digits in 2024.

item.caption:
🗳️ Election Day is just 8 days away!

Make your voice heard in the November 3 election! To help ensure your ballot is counted, return it to one of Douglas County’s convenient 24-hour ballot drop box locations.

📍 Find a drop box near you:

Douglas County Courthouse — 213 S Rainier Street, Waterville

Law & Justice Center — 100 19th Street NW, East Wenatchee

Office of Public Defense — 110 2nd Street NE, East Wenatchee

East Wenatchee City Hall — 271 9th Street NE, East Wenatchee

Rock Island City Hall — 5 N Garden Avenue, Rock Island

Bridgeport City Hall — 1206 Columbia Avenue, Bridgeport

Mansfield City Hall — 26 Main Street, Mansfield

Coulee Dam Town Hall — 300 Lincoln Avenue, Coulee Dam

⏰ Important reminder: All ballot drop boxes close at 8 p.m. on Election Day, November 3.

Don't wait until the last minute. Return your ballot on time and make your vote heard!

For more information visit: https://www.douglascountywa.gov/201/Elections

#DouglasCountyWA #ElectionDay #MakeYourVoteHeard

item.caption:
• Petsa: Oktubre 27, 2026
• Layunin: Upang ihalal ang lahat ng 120 miyembro ng unicameral na parlamento ng Israel (ang Knesset) at palitan ang ika-37 pamahalaan/administrasyon ni Netanyahu.
• Kahalagahan: Ito ang unang pangkalahatang halalan na idaraos matapos ang mga pag-atake noong Oktubre 7, ang digmaan sa Gaza, at mga tunggalian sa rehiyon; ito rin ang unang pagkakataon mula noong 1988 na nakumpleto ng ika-25 Knesset ang buong apat na taong termino nang hindi ito binuwag nang maaga.
• Sistemang Elektoral: Proportional representation na may electoral threshold na 3.25%, kung saan 38 partido ang kalahok sa pinal na balota.
• Kwalipikasyon ng mga Botante: Mga mamamayan ng Israel na rehistradong residente at sasapit sa edad na 18 sa araw ng halalan o bago pa man ito.

Tara let's go & Vote. #ElectionKnesset26th #ElectionDay #electiondayisrael #tuesdayvibes #votingday

item.caption:
@judy5203 Section 9-102 details the required order of steps once polls close (typically 9:00 p.m. on Election Day, after anyone already in line has voted):
•  Station an inspector at the ballot scanner to prevent further voting.
•  Reconcile paper ballots.

author: cherae2018

item.caption:
I VOTED TODAY! 🗳️❤️

I vote because there was a time when people who looked like me didn’t have the same right.

I vote because Black men weren’t constitutionally protected from racial discrimination in voting until 1870, with the passage of the 15th Amendment.

I vote because women didn’t gain nationwide constitutional protection for their right to vote until 1920, with the passage of the 19th Amendment.

I vote because even after those amendments, Black Americans continued to face barriers to voting, leading to the Voting Rights Act of 1965.

As a Black woman, I understand that the right I exercised today was fought for by generations before me.

I vote because they couldn’t. I vote because they fought. I vote because I can. ✊🏾❤️

#IVoted #BlackWomenVote #VotingRights #OurVoicesMatter #LakeCountyVotes

Today is Vote Early Day, a reminder that making your voice heard doesn't have to wait until Election Day! The Beverly Hills West (CA) Chapter of The Links, Incorporated encourages all eligible voters to explore their voting options and choose the method that works best for them.

California voters can return their completed ballots by mail, at an official voting location or by dropping in an official ballot drop box. Or you can vote early in person at participating locations or on Election Day November 3.

Already voted? Encourage a friend, family member or neighbor to make their plan, too! Your voice matters every day, not just on Election Day.

Find early voting locations and ballot drop boxes at caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov.

item.caption:
🇺🇸 I VOTED! 🗳️

In his Gettysburg Address, Abraham Lincoln spoke of a nation dedicated to the principle that all people are created equal and a government “of the people, by the people, for the people.”

Those words, spoken more than 160 years ago, still carry tremendous meaning today.

Our democracy is something worth preserving, but it requires more than words. It requires participation.

Regardless of our political beliefs or the candidates we support, we each have a voice and a responsibility to help shape the future of our communities, our state, and our nation.

A government of the people, by the people, and for the people is only possible when we, the people, exercise our right to vote.

🇺🇸 I exercised that right today, and I encourage you to do the same.

Your voice matters. Your vote matters.

#IVoted #YourVoteMatters #GetOutAndVote #WeThePeople #CivicDuty

item.caption:
So many people paid a price for me to have this right. The women who marched, were jailed, and some who died fighting so women like me could have a voice. The servicemen and women who left their families, served far from home, and some who never came back.They gave so much so I could walk in and make my voice heard. Not voting is shameful when you think about what it cost them. Staying home would feel like spitting in their face, and I refuse to do that.

So I showed up. Not because it was convenient, but because it matters, and because they mattered. If you haven’t yet, make your plan and honor them with your vote. 

#IVoted #HonorTheirSacrifice #WomensSuffrage #ThankAVeteran #CivicDuty

author: npr

item.caption:
The midterm election is a week from today, although early voting has been underway.

A new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll finds that, among “likely voters,” Democrats have an 8-point advantage on the congressional ballot. Respondents were asked whom they would vote for if the election were today in their district. Many observers say they expect Democrats will win control of the House of Representatives, although the size of any Democratic victory in the House isn't known — and the Senate is a toss-up.

Clarification: The headline of this video has been updated to more accurately represent the results of the NPR/PBS News/Marist poll.

Find “NPR News Now” wherever you listen to podcasts.

Host: Korva Coleman/NPR
Reporter: Domenico Montanaro/NPR
Producer: Zayrha Rodriguez/NPR

Voting is more than a right. It’s a responsibility and an opportunity to influence the decisions that shape our lives and the future of generations coming behind us.

We don’t have to agree on candidates, policies, or political perspectives to recognize the importance of exercising our constitutional rights.

Leadership isn’t just about having a voice. It’s about taking responsibility for how you use it.

Don’t just talk about what needs to change. Take part in the process!

✅ I DID MY PART!

🇺🇸 Your Voice. Your Choice. Your Vote. EVERY VOTE COUNTS!

item.caption:
With a week to go before Nov. 3, a few rules are worth knowing before you head to the polls. If your name isn't on the voter list, the federal Help America Vote Act lets you cast a provisional ballot, which is counted once officials confirm you're eligible, and if you're in line when the polls close, stay in line, because you're still allowed to vote. Results may take time in some places: each state sets its own counting rules, and states including Pennsylvania and Wisconsin don't let officials start processing mail ballots until Election Day. Check your registration, polling place and ID rules at vote.gov or your state election office.

#KnowYourRights #Vote #2026Midterms #ElectionDay #AgoraNow

Election Day Is Nov. 3rd and Secretary Howden Encourages Texans to Vote with Confidence

With Election Day for the November General Election one week away, Texas Secretary of State Robert S. Howden encouraged eligible Texans who have not yet voted to confirm their polling location and prepare to cast a ballot on or before Nov. 3.

Learn more at texasborderbusiness.com, link in bio.

🗳️ YOUR VOICE MATTERS. YOUR VOTE MATTERS! 🇺🇸

Election Day is Tuesday, November 3rd! Don’t wait until the last minute to make your voice heard. ❤️🤍💙

✅ Fill out your ballot. ✅ SIGN your return envelope! 🖊️ ✅ SEAL your envelope. ✅ Take it to an OFFICIAL ballot drop box yourself to make sure it gets there on time!

📅 DEADLINE: Tuesday, November 3rd, by 8:00 PM for official drop boxes in Washington State.

Your vote is your voice, and every step matters! Encourage your family, friends, and community to participate, too. 🙌🏾

DON’T JUST TALK ABOUT IT—VOTE! 🗳️

item.caption:
Why do Americans vote on a Tuesday? 🗳️ One law from 1845 picked the day, and it never says why. Before it, each state chose its own day inside a 34-day window. The act's rule: "the Tuesday next after the first Monday in the month of November." The farm and Sabbath story is the usual explanation, written later. The rule is still federal law, and since the 1870s it sets House elections too; this year it's November 3.
What surprised you most? 1 A MONTH-LONG ELECTION / 2 STILL LAW 181 YEARS ON / 3 A LAW THAT NEVER SAYS WHY. Comment 1, 2 or 3.
Document cards are styled reconstructions of the act; paintings by George Caleb Bingham, shown for the period, not as 1844 scenes; AI voice.
#ElectionDay #History #USHistory #Elections #HistoryFacts
